title.en: Some, any, no, none and compounds
title.es: Some, any, no, none y sus compuestos

summary.en: Use **some** in positive sentences and in offers or requests; use **any** in negatives, in most questions and to mean "it doesn't matter which". **No** and **none** already make a sentence negative, so never add **not**. The same pattern applies to the compounds: _something / anything / nothing_, _somebody / anybody / nobody_, _somewhere / anywhere / nowhere_.
summary.es: En inglés solo hay una negación por frase: «no conozco a nadie» = I don't know anybody (o I know nobody), nunca I don't know nobody.

form: **some** + plural or uncountable (positive, offers, requests): _some water, some ideas_
**any** + plural or uncountable (negatives, questions, if): _I haven't got any time._
**no** + noun = not any: _There is no milk._ **None** stands alone or is followed by of: _None of them came._
**something / somebody / somewhere**, **anything / anybody / anywhere**, **nothing / nobody / nowhere**
**any** (free choice, stressed) = whichever: _Any day is fine._

uses.text: **Positive statements** → some: _I bought some bread._ _She's meeting somebody at six._
**Offers and requests** → some: _Would you like some tea?_ _Could I have some information?_
**Negatives and questions** → any: _We didn't see anyone._ _Is there anything I can do?_

note.en: With a negative verb, use any- words; with a positive verb, use no- words. Never both.
note.es: Verbo negativo + any-; verbo afirmativo + no-. Nunca las dos negaciones.

uses.text: **Nothing available** → no / none: _There are no rooms left._ _How many did you buy? None._
**Free choice** → any: _You can ask any of the staff._ _Take any seat you like._

mistakes.wrong: I don't know nothing about the project.
mistakes.right: I don't know anything about the project. / I know nothing about the project.

why.en: English allows only one negative word in a clause.
why.es: No se acumulan negaciones: don't + anything, o bien nothing.

mistakes.wrong: Nobody didn't call me this morning.

why.en: Nobody is already negative, so the verb stays positive.
why.es: «Nadie me llamó» lleva el verbo en afirmativo.

why.en: In a neutral question, use any; some suggests you expect a yes.
why.es: En preguntas neutras se usa any.

mistakes.wrong: No of my colleagues speak German.
mistakes.right: None of my colleagues speak German.

why.en: Before of, use none, not no.
why.es: Ante of se usa none; no va directamente antes de un sustantivo.

mistakes.wrong: There aren't no seats at the back.
mistakes.right: There aren't any seats at the back. / There are no seats at the back.

why.en: Use not + any, or no with a positive verb.

examples.en: We can't make dinner tonight. There isn't anything in the fridge.
examples.es: Esta noche no podemos hacer la cena. No hay nada en la nevera.

examples.en: Would you like some more coffee?
I looked everywhere, but I couldn't find my glasses anywhere.
Somebody has left a bag on the platform.
There was nobody at the front desk, so I waited.
None of the candidates had any experience in sales.
You can pay by card or in cash. Any method is fine.
We've got no time left, so let's decide now.
Is there anywhere quiet where we can talk?
If you have any questions, please ask.

practice.prompt: I haven't seen ___ of my cousins this year.

explanation.en: After a negative verb we use any; none would make a double negative.

practice.prompt: Could you lend me ___ money until Friday?

explanation.en: A request takes some, even though it is a question.

practice.prompt: We can't cook tonight. There isn't ___ in the fridge.

explanation.en: With the negative isn't we use anything, not nothing.

practice.prompt: Did any of the applicants have experience? No, ___ of them did.

explanation.en: None of them is the pattern; no and nobody cannot be followed by of them.

practice.prompt: You can choose ___ colour you like; they are all in stock.

explanation.en: Any means "whichever you like" when the choice is free.
